==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{a|en|UK}} ** {{enPR|bŏrʹō|a=RP}}; {{IPA|en|/ˈbɒɹəʊ/}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈbɒɹə/|a=Northumbria}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈbɔɹo/|a=Scotland}} * {{enPR|bärʹō|a=GA,CA}}; {{IPA|en|/ˈbɑɹ.oʊ/}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-borrow.ogg|a=US}} * {{enPR|bôrʹo|bōrʹō|a=dialect}}; {{IPA|en|/ˈboɹ.oʊ/}} * {{rhymes|en|ɒɹəʊ|s=2}} * {{hyphenation|en|bor|row}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰergʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|borwen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|borgian||to borrow, lend, pledge surety for}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*borgōn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*burgōną||to pledge, take care of}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰergʰ-||to take care}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|borgen||to borrow, trust}}, {{cog|de|borgen||to borrow, lend}}, {{cog|da|borge||to vouch}}. Related to {{cog|ang|beorgan||to save, preserve}}. More at {{m|en|bury}}. ====Alternative forms==== * {{alt|en|boro||Jamaican English}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # To [[receive]] (something) from somebody temporarily, expecting to [[return]] it. #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-01|volume=407|issue=8838|page=71| title=[http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21578670-peer-peer-lending-needs-new-name-end-peer-show End of the peer show]| passage=Finance is seldom romantic. But the idea of peer-to-peer lending comes close. This is an industry that brings together individual savers and lenders on online platforms. Those that want to '''borrow''' are matched with those that want to lend.}} # To receive money from a bank or other lender under the agreement that the lender will be paid back over time. # To adopt (an idea) as one's own. #: {{co|en|to '''borrow''' the style, manner, or opinions of another}} #* {{RQ:Milton Eikonoklastes|passage=It is not hard for any man, who hath a Bible in his hands, to '''borrow''' good words and holy sayings in abundance; but to make them his own is a work of grace only from above.}} #* {{quote-book |en |author = w:William Minto; Margaret Bryant |title = Encyclopædia Britannica, Ninth Edition |url = https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica,_Ninth_Edition |year = 1881 |entry = John Dryden |passage = Dryden’s form is of course '''borrowed''' from the ancients}} # {{senseid|en|linguistics}} {{lb|en|linguistics}} To adopt a word from another language. #* {{RQ:Guardian|date=2024-06-20|author=Eva Corlett|title=Fidlets, fingies and riding a doo: study sheds light on Antarctic English slang|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/jun/20/fidlets-fingies-and-riding-a-doo-antarctica-english-slang-terms|passage=Americans, for example, call newcomers to Antarctica “fingies”, which comes from FNGs – a '''borrowed''' military abbreviation that means “Fucking New Guy”.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013073203/https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/jun/20/fidlets-fingies-and-riding-a-doo-antarctica-english-slang-terms|archivedate=13 October 2026}} # {{lb|en|arithmetic}} In absolute value [[subtraction]], to deduct (one) from a digit of the number with the overall larger value and add ten to the following digit, in order that the subtraction of a larger digit in the number with the overall smaller value does not yield a combination of negative and positive numbers in the same answer. # {{senseid|en|lend}} {{lb|en|Upper Midwestern US|West Midlands|Malaysia|Singapore|proscribed}} To [[lend]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1951|year_published=1998|publisher=University of Wisconsin Press| editor=James P. Leary|author=The Grenadiers| section=Milwaukee Talk| isbn=9780299160340| page=56| title=[http://books.google.com/books?id=42NjCJe6xYEC&pg=PA56&dq=%22borrow+me+your%22&lr=&as_brr=3&cd=13#v=onepage&q=%22borrow%20me%20your%22&f=false Wisconsin Folklore]| passage=“Rosie, '''borrow''' me your look looker, I bet my lips are all. Everytime{{sic}} I eat or drink, so quick I gotta fix ’em, yet.”}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1987|author=w:Michael Chiang|title=Army Daze|location=Singapore|isbn=9789971652258|publisher=Landmark Books|text={{smc|Johari Salleh:}} [[ya#Etymology 2|Ya]], ya. Better not waste time. Must prepare, tomorrow morning [[got#Etymology 2|got]] inspection.
{{smc|Teo Ah Beng:}} Ya {{l|en|lah#Etymology 2|id=colloquialize}}, must [[kiwi#Etymology 2|kiwi]] [polish] the boots. Can '''borrow''' me your cloth?
{{smc|Krishnamoorthy:}} Ya, no problem. You better kiwi quickly. 11 pm lights off. {{...}}}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2007|publisher=Lulu.com|author=Silvia Cecchini| title=[http://books.google.com/books?id=drdzm3jr81kC&pg=PA7&dq=%22borrow+me+your%22&lr=&as_brr=3&cd=22#v=onepage&q=%22borrow%20me%20your%22&f=false Bach Flowers Fairytales]| isbn=9781847533203| page=7| passage=“Gaia, could you '''borrow''' me your pencils ,{{SIC}} today, if you do not use them?”}} # {{lb|en|ditransitive}} To temporarily obtain (something) for (someone). # To feign or counterfeit. #* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=III|canto=XII|stanza=14|passage='''borrowed''' hair}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare King John|I|i|passage=the '''borrowed''' majesty of England}} # {{lb|en|obsolete|_|except in ballads}} To secure the release of (someone) from prison. # {{lb|en|informal}} To [[receive]] (something, usually of trifling value) from somebody, with little possibility of returning it. #: {{ux|en|Can I '''borrow''' a sheet of paper?}} # {{lb|en|informal}} To interrupt the current activity of (a person) and lead them away in order to speak with them, get their help, etc. #: {{ux|en|John, can I '''borrow''' you for a second? I need your help with the copier.}} # {{lb|en|golf}} To [[adjust]] one's [[aim]] in order to [[compensate]] for the [[slope]] of the [[green]]. =====Conjugation===== {{en-conj|old=1}} Thomas|title=Golf Architecture in America: Its Strategy and Construction |passage={{...}} slippery contours, so that in making a side hill putt more than the usual amount of '''borrow''' had to be considered.}} # {{lb|en|construction|civil engineering}} A [[borrow pit]]. #* {{quote-journal|en|year=1979|journal=The Canadian Mining and Metallurgical Bulletin |passage=As previously indicated, slurry used for construction of the slurry cutoff trench at Beaver Creek Dam was produced with natural clays and clay tills from local '''borrows'''.}} # {{lb|en|programming}} In [[Rust]] and some other programming languages, the situation where the [[ownership]] of a [[value]] is temporarily transferred to another region of code. =====Translations===== {{trans-top|deviation of a rolling golfball}} * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Irish: {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 2=== From {{inh|en|enm|borwe}}, {{m|enm|borgh}}, from {{inh|en|ang|borh}}, {{m|ang|borg}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*borgōn}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*burgōną|t=to borrow, lend}} (related to Etymology 1, above). ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} {{lb|en|archaic}} # A [[ransom]]; a [[pledge]] or [[guarantee]]. # A [[surety]]; someone standing [[bail]].
